display_name: Slow heel tap from a step
description: A controlled single-leg eccentric exercise improving quad strength, knee tracking, and balance.
setup: Stand on a sturdy low step or bench with one foot planted on the edge and the other foot hovering off the side.
steps: Shift your weight onto the standing leg with hands out in front for balance.
Slowly bend the standing knee and push hips back to lower the hovering foot.
Gently tap the floor with the hovering heel without shifting weight onto it.
Push through the midfoot of the standing leg to return to full extension.
cues: Keep the standing knee tracking directly over your second toe
Tap the ground lightly like touching eggshells with your heel

mistakes.mistake: Pushing off the floor with the bottom foot
mistakes.fix: Keep heel light and do all the work with the elevated leg

mistakes.mistake: Standing knee caving inward toward midline
mistakes.fix: Engage glute medius to keep knee aligned over your toes

rep_standard: Begins standing on top of step, lowers with control until free heel taps floor, and returns to full single-leg standing extension.
